name: Reflexion: Self-Critique Loop for Candidate Generation
key_paper: Shinn, N., Cassano, F., Labash, B., Gopinath, A., Narasimhan, K., & Yao, S. (2023). Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning. NeurIPS 2023.
algorithm_description: Reflexion is a framework in which an agent generates a candidate output, receives a scalar or verbal evaluation signal, then produces a natural-language or structured self-critique that is appended to the context before the next generation attempt. The loop is: (1) Actor generates a candidate (e.g., a play), (2) Evaluator scores it against a heuristic or oracle, (3) Self-Reflection module verbalizes what was wrong and how to improve, (4) the critique is stored in a short-term memory buffer, and (5) the Actor re-generates conditioned on the critique. Unlike gradient-based RL the policy weights are not updated; improvement comes from in-context conditioning. In the lottery adaptation the verbal critique is replaced by a structured JSON critique (e.g., over-represented hot numbers, missing cold numbers, poor gap coverage) which is fed back into the generation prompt or used as a differentiable reward signal to re-rank candidates.
action_space_handling: Reflexion is action-space agnostic -- it does not sample from a parameterized distribution or compute policy gradients. The Actor can use any generation mechanism (temperature sampling, beam search, greedy decoding). In the lottery context the existing SharedLotteryTransformer produces 50 logits; Reflexion wraps the generation call in an iterative critique-and-revise loop. Each iteration the critique (e.g., 'numbers 3, 7, 14 appeared in 60% of recent draws -- reduce their weight') is encoded as a bias vector added to the logits before the next Gumbel top-k sample. The action space {1..50 choose 7} is explored across iterations rather than through stochastic sampling alone.
how_combinatorial_output_is_formed: Initial candidate generation uses the existing Gumbel top-k or temperature-softmax sampling from SharedLotteryTransformer logits. The Reflexion loop then evaluates the candidate against historical pattern heuristics (frequency deviation, gap analysis, number co-occurrence coverage) and computes a structured critique vector. On subsequent iterations the critique is operationalized as: (a) additive logit adjustments that down-weight over-represented numbers and up-weight under-represented numbers, or (b) a resampling call with a modified temperature and masked logits. The final accepted candidate is the one scoring highest on the composite heuristic after T iterations (typically T=3-5). This is analogous to best-of-T sampling guided by a learned or rule-based Evaluator.
sequential_generation_strategy: Reflexion operates at the play level rather than the number level -- each iteration generates a full set of k numbers simultaneously (flat multi-hot / joint strategy). The sequential dimension is across iterations of the critique loop, not within a single play. This means inter-number correlations within a play are only as well-modeled as the underlying Actor (the existing SharedLotteryTransformer multi-hot head). Adding autoregressive generation inside the Actor would capture within-play correlations but is orthogonal to the Reflexion outer loop. The iterative loop allows the play to shift holistically based on aggregate critiques (e.g., 'this play is too similar to the last 3 plays -- increase diversity').
gradient_estimator_type: None -- Reflexion does not backpropagate through the generation process. Improvement is achieved by conditioning the Actor on critique context, not by updating model weights. In the original LLM formulation critiques are verbal strings. In the lottery-nn adaptation critiques are structured scalar adjustments (logit biases or reward shaping signals). If the critique-to-logit adjustment is treated as a differentiable transformation, standard backpropagation through the bias addition is trivial; however this is a minor implementation detail rather than a gradient estimator in the RL sense. No REINFORCE, Gumbel-softmax, or straight-through estimator is involved.
combinatorial_constraint_enforcement: Constraint enforcement (exactly k distinct numbers from {1..N}) is delegated to the underlying Actor's sampling mechanism, exactly as in the baseline. Reflexion adds no new constraint-enforcement mechanism. After the critique adjusts the logits, the same Gumbel top-k or autoregressive masking sampler is applied to ensure exactly 7 distinct numbers from {1..50}. The critique itself can explicitly flag constraint violations (e.g., 'candidate contains number 51 -- out of range') as a safety check, but this is a degenerate case with a well-implemented Actor.
sample_efficiency_rating: high -- Reflexion is extremely sample-efficient because it does not require gradient updates from reward signals. Each iteration of the critique loop uses deterministic heuristics computed directly from the historical draw data (frequency tables, gap statistics, co-occurrence matrices), which can be computed exactly from even 50-100 draws. The iterative refinement extracts more value from each observed draw by applying multi-dimensional critique rather than a scalar reward. Empirically Shinn et al. (2023) showed Reflexion outperforms CoT baselines by 22% on HotpotQA with no additional training data. The lottery adaptation inherits this data efficiency: all critique heuristics are non-parametric statistics over the fixed draw history.
regularization_built_in: Reflexion's iterative critique loop provides implicit regularization through diversity enforcement: the Evaluator can explicitly penalize candidates that are too similar to previously generated plays (Jaccard overlap check) or that over-fit to the most recent draws (recency bias detection). No weight decay, dropout, or KL penalty is involved since no model weights are updated. The short-term memory buffer (storing critiques from prior iterations) acts as a form of population-level constraint, preventing the loop from cycling back to the same bad candidates. Entropy of the final play distribution across multiple Reflexion runs is naturally maintained if the Evaluator rewards coverage.
known_failure_modes_on_small_data: 1. Critique overfitting: with only 100 draws the frequency statistics used in the critique are noisy -- the Evaluator may penalize numbers that appear rare by chance rather than by true rarity, causing the critique loop to systematically avoid numbers with limited evidence. 2. Heuristic gaming: if the critique heuristics are based solely on historical frequency, the Actor learns to generate plays that look historically typical rather than informationally diverse -- critique-guided convergence to the empirical distribution rather than the generative process. 3. Loop divergence: if critique signals from successive iterations contradict each other (iteration 1: 'include more hot numbers'; iteration 2: 'reduce hot numbers'), the loop oscillates without converging. 4. Critique quality ceiling: rule-based critiques are limited by the quality of the heuristics; with 100 draws, pattern-based insights have wide confidence intervals and the critique may be uninformative or misleading.
data_regime_evidence: minimum_training_samples_tested: The original Reflexion paper (Shinn et al. 2023) used it on HotpotQA, AlfWorld, and HumanEval -- none of which are small-data RL settings in the traditional sense (the LLM already has extensive pretraining). The technique does not require a training set in the conventional sense -- it requires a scoring heuristic, which for lottery can be computed from any number of draws. Practical minimum: frequency tables are meaningful from ~50 draws; gap analysis from ~30 draws; co-occurrence statistics require ~200+ draws to be reliable. performance_degradation_curve: Critique quality (precision of the heuristic feedback) degrades with fewer draws, but the loop still functions; the risk is that poor critiques add noise rather than signal. comparison_baseline: Reflexion-style iterative refinement is expected to outperform single-shot temperature sampling at any data scale because it can always fall back to heuristic critique even with zero draws (using prior knowledge about lottery statistics). [uncertain]
convergence_guarantees_small_n: No formal convergence guarantees exist for Reflexion as a non-gradient method. The loop terminates after a fixed number of iterations T (typically 3-5) rather than by convergence criterion. Within T iterations, monotone improvement is guaranteed only if the Evaluator is a consistent and complete scorer -- in practice with noisy heuristics this is not assured. For the lottery case the composite heuristic score (frequency deviation + gap score + diversity penalty) can be made monotone per iteration by design, but the resulting play is a local optimum of the heuristic, not necessarily a better lottery pick. Shinn et al. show empirical improvement on benchmark tasks without theoretical guarantees. [uncertain]
reward_distribution_handling: Reflexion decouples the critique signal from the sparse end-of-episode reward. The Evaluator in the lottery context uses dense intermediate signals (frequency statistics, gap coverage, co-occurrence scores) rather than waiting for the weekly draw outcome. This effectively replaces the extremely sparse {0, 1, 2, ..., 7} hit-count reward with a dense multi-dimensional critique score computed immediately from historical data. This is a major advantage over gradient-based RL methods that must wait for actual draw outcomes. The iterative refinement loop can incorporate the actual draw result when available (post-draw critique: 'play missed numbers in the 30-40 range which appeared -- next iteration should cover that gap') as a form of delayed Reflexion.
credit_assignment_granularity: Reflexion naturally supports number-level credit assignment through the structured critique. The Evaluator can analyze each individual number in the candidate play: is number i over-represented in recent draws? does the pair (i, j) co-occur too often in the play? is number i in a cold streak? This per-number critique is richer than the play-level scalar reward of vanilla RL -- it is semi-bandit feedback built into the Evaluator design rather than extracted from a gradient estimator. The critique can explicitly identify which k numbers should be swapped and which k numbers should be added, giving direct number-level guidance without requiring a differentiable reward decomposition.
diversity_mechanism: Reflexion supports explicit diversity enforcement through the Evaluator: a critique can penalize plays that are too similar to previously accepted plays (Jaccard similarity > threshold), forcing the Actor to explore different number combinations across iterations. Additionally, across multiple Reflexion runs (each generating one play), the short-term memory buffer stores all previously accepted plays and the Evaluator can reject candidates that overlap with them. This is more principled than entropy bonuses or temperature scaling because diversity is enforced at the play-set level rather than at the per-number probability level. For a 5-play ticket, 5 sequential Reflexion runs with a diversity penalty in the Evaluator guarantee that no two plays share more than floor(k/2) numbers.
offline_vs_online_rl_compatibility: Fully offline -- Reflexion requires no online environment interaction for the critique loop itself. All heuristics (frequency tables, gap statistics, co-occurrence matrices) are precomputed from the fixed historical draw dataset and do not require waiting for new draws. The post-draw update (incorporating the actual result into the critique memory) is optional and additive -- the system degrades gracefully to pure heuristic-based critique when no new draws are available. This is the best possible offline compatibility among all Phase 2 candidates: the loop runs entirely at prediction time using existing data, with zero online RL overhead.
key_dependencies: No additional libraries required beyond PyTorch and numpy (for heuristic statistics). Optional: pandas (already present in lottery-nn) for frequency table computation. No stable-baselines3, torchrl, pyro, or RL framework required. The Evaluator is a pure Python function computing statistics over draws.csv. If the critique is verbalized as natural language (LLM-in-the-loop), an Anthropic API call would be needed, but the structured critique variant requires no LLM.
estimated_lines_of_code: 120-180 lines of new code: ~40 lines for the Evaluator (frequency deviation, gap score, diversity penalty), ~30 lines for the critique-to-logit-adjustment function, ~30 lines for the Reflexion loop (T iterations, short-term memory buffer), ~20 lines for integration into main_swarm.py predict path. Excludes existing src/analysis.py helpers that are directly reusable as Evaluator components.
transfer_learning_compatibility: Fully compatible -- Reflexion wraps the existing SharedLotteryTransformer as a black box and does not modify its weights. The pretrained shared encoder and per-lottery output heads are used exactly as trained; Reflexion only modifies the logits at inference time (additive critique bias) and wraps the sampling call in an iterative loop. No fine-tuning, gradient updates, or architectural changes are required. The existing src/analysis.py frequency_table(), hot_cold(), pair_frequency(), and gap_analysis() helpers are directly reusable as Evaluator components, further reducing implementation effort.
specific_application_in_project: Reflexion is the most immediately implementable Phase 2 component and directly implements the 'Actor-Critic play generation' loop described in CLAUDE.md. Concrete implementation: (1) Actor: existing SharedLotteryTransformer produces logits for the requested lottery (lottomax/649/dailygrand); (2) Evaluator: a new src/evaluator.py module computes a structured critique dict from the candidate play using helpers from src/analysis.py -- fields include frequency_deviation (how much each number deviates from its historical frequency), gap_score (are the numbers spread across the {1..50} range?), recency_bias (do any numbers have cold streaks longer than X draws?), and diversity_penalty (Jaccard overlap with already-accepted plays in this session); (3) Reflexion loop in src/reflexion.py: for T=3 iterations, convert critique to an additive logit bias vector and resample; (4) Accept the play with the highest composite Evaluator score across all T iterations; (5) Integration: main_swarm.py predict calls reflexion.generate_play() instead of predict.generate_play(). This replaces the static temperature-softmax sampling in src/predict.py with an iterative critique-guided refinement. All three lotteries benefit equally. Phase 2 implementation estimated at 1-2 days.
replaces_or_extends: Extends -- replaces temperature-softmax sampling in src/predict.py with a Reflexion-guided iterative sampling loop while keeping the SharedLotteryTransformer encoder and output heads unchanged. The Evaluator adds a new scoring layer on top of the existing src/analysis.py statistical helpers. No existing component is removed.
existing_open_source_implementations: 1. Official Reflexion repo: noahshinn/reflexion (GitHub, 2023) -- Python implementation for HotpotQA, AlfWorld, HumanEval; uses LLM for both Actor and Self-Reflection. 2. LangChain ReflexionAgent (langchain/agents/reflexion) -- production-ready wrapper, adds overhead of LangChain dependency. 3. AutoGPT and BabyAGI both implement iterative self-critique loops structurally similar to Reflexion without the verbal RL framing. 4. For the structured (non-LLM) variant relevant to lottery-nn there is no off-the-shelf implementation -- the critique is a domain-specific heuristic function rather than a language model, making a custom implementation (~150 lines) more appropriate than adapting the LLM-centric repos.
benchmark_results: Shinn et al. (2023) NeurIPS: HotpotQA question answering -- Reflexion outperforms CoT by 22% (pass@1 accuracy); HumanEval Python coding -- Reflexion with GPT-4 achieves 91% pass@1 vs 80% for GPT-4 alone (11pp gain); AlfWorld sequential decision making -- 97% task completion vs 75% for ReAct baseline. All benchmarks use LLM actors. For the structured-critique variant (no LLM): iterative best-of-T sampling with a domain heuristic scorer consistently outperforms single-shot sampling by the margin of the heuristic precision -- no formal benchmark exists for lottery-scale data, but the technique is a standard component of combinatorial optimization solvers (simulated annealing, iterated local search). [uncertain]
notable_use_cases: 1. HumanEval code generation (Shinn et al. 2023): generate code, run unit tests, critique errors, revise -- structurally identical to generate play, evaluate against historical heuristics, critique, revise. 2. Iterative molecular design (Gao et al. 2022, REINVENT): generate molecular candidate, score against docking/ADMET heuristics, revise SMILES -- closest structural analog to generate lottery play, score against statistical patterns, revise. 3. AlphaCode / Codex iterative sampling: generate N candidates, re-rank by test-case pass rate -- equivalent to generating T plays and accepting the highest-scoring one after Reflexion critique. 4. Constrained text generation with iterative constraint checking (Lu et al. 2022, Neurologic Decoding): generate candidate, check combinatorial constraints, revise -- directly analogous to checking lottery play against frequency/gap/diversity constraints. 5. Combinatorial auction bidding with iterative refinement (Dutting et al. 2019): generate bid set, evaluate against value function, revise -- same iterative combinatorial selection pattern.
